{{Quote|The Tal Nami have a very interesting culture.|DV-9|<ref name="GoF2" />}}
The '''Tal Nami''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tal Nami]] in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]]. They were [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] species but were renowned for loathing their masters. To survive, members of the species needed to consume both the [[Fruit/Legends|fruit]] of the [[egoa tree]] and the roots of the [[capabara plant]] as part of their regular [[Diet/Legends|diet]]. As the two [[Foodstuff/Legends|foods]] only grew in different regions of the species' [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], the Tal Nami developed a rigid honor system for trading. The species became known as avid [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]] and haters of those who traded unfairly.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Their bodies need two foods to survive&mdash;the fruit of the egoa tree and the root of the capabara plant.|DV-9 explains the Tal Nami's dietary needs|<ref name="GoF2" />}}
The Tal Nami were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that evolved on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tal Nami]] in the [[Tal Nami system/Legends|system of the same name]]. Members of the species required two specific elements in their [[Diet/Legends|diet]] to survive: the [[Fruit/Legends|fruit]] of the [[egoa tree]] and the root of the [[capabara plant]]. Individual Tal Nami had both [[Limb/Legends|feet]] and hands.<ref name="GoF2" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|In order to prevent the entire population from starving, they have developed a code of honor among traders. Each trader tries to make sure the other one gets the better end of the bargain. Since both sides are doing this, it assures a fair trade.|DV-9 explains Tal Nami culture|<ref name="GoF2" />}}
[[File:Hutt-NEGAS.png|thumb|left|300px|alt=A Hutt with a datapad stares slyly over their shoulder.|The Tal Nami hated the Hutts for enslaving them.]]
Tal Nami were considered avid [[Merchant/Legends|traders]],<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> a reputation that, like other aspects of their culture, developed partially due their dietary needs for survival. The two [[Plant/Legends|plants]] they required grew only in two separate regions of their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], both of which were inhabited by different groups of Tal Nami. Both populations relied on the other for their supply of the vital [[Foodstuff/Legends|foodstuff]] they cultivated; so, to ensure that neither population starved, the species established a code of honor concerning trade. Its strictures stated that merchants had to do their best to ensure that they gave the better end of the bargain to any being with whom they traded. This ensured that the two populations both received a fair bargain, as each population's traders attempted to give the better deal to traders from the other population.<ref name="GoF2" />

Merchants found to be trading unfairly within Tal Nami society were punished. The punishment consisted of the trader's hands and feet being tied to an egoa [[Tree/Legends|tree]]: the hands were bound to the branches and the feet to the roots. Due to the rapid growth rate of the egoa tree&mdash;it grew at a rate of one [[Meter/Legends|meter]] per [[Standard day/Legends|day]]&mdash;the individual was [[Death/Legends|torn apart]]. Members of the species had an intense dislike of any trader they believed to engage in unfair dealing, and they pursued such individuals across great distances through [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to punish them.<ref name="GoF2" /> The Tal Nami's hatred extended to the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] species, who had [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] them, since the Hutts were renowned as sly and untrustworthy businessbeings and criminals. Despite their own slave status, Tal Nami openly admitted their loathing of the Hutts,<ref name="EA" /> although they paid tribute to their masters.<ref name="TOR">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Underworld Trading|Tribute}}</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Did you say they'd travel light-years to track down&hellip;|Used starship salesman Meego considers the consequences of angering the Tal Nami|<ref name="GoF2" />}}
[[File:D-V9.jpg|thumb|right|250px|alt=The white protocol droid DV-9 stands with a human visible in the foreground and a gray structure visible behind him.|DV-9 was familiar with the Tal Nami's culture.]]
The Tal Nami homeworld was considered part of the region of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] known as [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] as early as [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]]. The Hutt species, who controlled Hutt Space, enslaved the Tal Nami, although the slaves became renowned for openly loathing their masters.<ref name="EA" /> Around the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3643 BBY]], the Tal Nami were late in offering a tribute they owed to the Hutts, and the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]], a Hutt criminal organization, paid individuals involved in underworld trading to find out why. The individuals met with the Tal Nami, who welcomed them and gave what tribute they could, promising more when it was available, as they did not want to anger their masters.<ref name="TOR" /> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the [[G9 Rigger-class light freighter/Legends|G9 Rigger-class light freighter]] ''[[Twilight]]'' was equipped with a Tal Nami [[Freighter/Legends|freighter's]] [[Tal Nami Freighter Swing Wing|swing wing]] which gave it greater maneuverability.<ref name="TCWVD">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]''</ref>

Prior to the year [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the Tal Nami developed a code of honor amongst their traders to ensure that all members of the species received dietary requirements they needed to survive while punishing any trader found to be dealing unfairly. In 0 ABY, the [[Biological science droid|research droid]] [[DV-9]] scared the used [[Starship/Legends|starship]] trader [[Meego]] into selling a vessel known as the [[Shroud (starship)|''Shroud'']] to him for a fair price by mentioning the Tal Nami's code of honor and their habit of hunting down unfair traders of whom they learned. The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] informed Meego that his master and the intended owner of the ship, the [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]], visited friends on Tal Nami often and planned to visit again soon. The droid suggested that certain Tal Nami might see the ship and learn of the way Meego had done business with the [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]].<ref name="GoF2" /> Tal Nami was still considered part of Hutt Space as late as [[137 ABY]].<ref name="EA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Tal Nami were first mentioned in the [[1997]] novel ''[[Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead]]'', which was part of the ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Fear]]'' series written by [[John Whitman]].<ref name="GoF2" />
